target_customer: Recreational and competitive shooters, ranges and trainers buying connected targets
problem: Static targets give shooters no instant feedback. LitHit targets light up on impact and connect to a phone for analytics and games.
business_model: Hardware sales of smart targets with companion app

founders.name: Anthony Crivolio
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no background.

founders.name: Eric Mills
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no background.

competitors.name: Autonomous Alloys (Digital Steel)
competitors.what: App connected steel shooting targets with backlit light bars and magnetic resetting
competitors.traction_then: Hit its $100,000 Indiegogo goal in under 3 days

technical_complexity.rationale: Impact sensing, lighting, wireless sync and an app are standard embedded engineering, but ruggedizing a target that takes fire is hard for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Several rivals sold app connected light up targets, and the concept was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Larger gun and accessory brands later shipped connected products such as SIG Connect. No acquisition of LitHit was found.

market_need_then: Shooting sports have a large hobby base and growing interest in connected training, but no source gives spend or complaint data for this wedge.

identity.visual_style: product led, tagline Light up on impact

branding.brand_signature: Targets that light up on impact

brand_strength.rationale: The name describes the product action, but no press or community about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: LitHit was a two person hardware team that took the standard YC seed in 2017 and never announced a later round. The company website still showed a 2017 copyright, which points to little activity afterward. The cause of the inactive status is not public, and rivals with similar light up targets existed before the batch.
notes: The seed round and investor rest on CB Insights alone; one other CB Insights page lists different investors (Praesidian Capital, Gemini Investors), which conflicts. CB Insights also names Avshalom Ehrlich or Jinesh Patel as founders, which conflicts with the YC page. True Aim Targets (August 2017) came about five months after the batch and is not listed. No outcome or shutdown coverage was found.
